Significant Earthquake Dataset

Source: R/data.R
globalearthquake.Rd

A data set containing the earthquakes of magnitude at least 5 that occurred during the period 1900-2022, with their GPS coordinates and magnitudes.

Usage

globalearthquake

Format

A data frame with 98785 rows and 12 variables:

date_time

date and time in POSIXct format

latitude

latitude of the earthquake, from -90° to 90°

longitude

longitude of the earthquake, from -180° to 180°

mag

the magnitude of the earthquake, indicating its strength

Date

date when the earthquake occurred

nbweeks

number of complete weeks elapsed since 1900/01/01

year

year

month

month of the year

month_day

day of the month

week

week of the year, from 1 to 53 (week 1 consists of the first seven days of the year, week 2 of the next seven days, etc.)

week_day

day of the week from 1 = Sunday to 7 = Saturday

year_day

day of the year from 1 to 366

Source

Earthquake Catalog, U.S. Geological Survey, Department of the Interior. https://www.usgs.gov/programs/earthquake-hazards

Details

This is a compiled version of the full data set available on U.S. Geological Survey Earthquake Events (USGS) which is in the public domain.

The data set contains only the earthquakes between 1900 and 2022 with a magnitude of at least 5, sorted by date and time.

Examples

summary(globalearthquake$mag)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   5.000   5.100   5.300   5.456   5.700   9.500 
## earthquakes in a rectangle around Japan since 1980
japan <- subset(
  globalearthquake,
  latitude > 30 & latitude < 46 & longitude > 129 & longitude < 146 &
    year >= 1980
)
## binary time series: was there at least one earthquake during the week?
weeks <- seq(min(japan$nbweeks), max(globalearthquake$nbweeks))
japan_weeks <- weeks %in% japan$nbweeks
table(japan_weeks)
#> japan_weeks
#> FALSE  TRUE 
#>   827  1417 
japan_model <- tune_vlmc(japan_weeks)
draw(as_vlmc(japan_model))
#> ▪ (0.3685, 0.6315)
#> └─ TRUE (0.3503, 0.6497)
#>    ├─ FALSE (0.4153, 0.5847)
#>    └─ TRUE (0.3156, 0.6844)
#>       └─ FALSE (0.4034, 0.5966)
